name: NY-14
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+19 district with a high-profile incumbent seeking re-election
Overwhelming money edge: $37.4M raised and $17.4M on hand vs. $0.4M for Hysenaj
Prediction markets price the race at roughly 97% Democratic
No public polls or expert ratings; forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's 19-point Democratic lean, Ocasio-Cortez's incumbency and national profile, and a roughly 90-to-1 fundraising advantage over Diamant Hysenaj all point the same direction, and markets price her win probability near 97%. With no opposing outside spending or contrary polling, the fundamentals justify a Safe D rating near a 26-point margin.
model.watch: With no public polling in the race, a late surge in challenger fundraising or a sharp shift in the national environment would be the main signals to watch.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez seeks re-election in a New York City district that leans Democratic by 19 points. She enters the general election with an enormous financial advantage, having raised $37.4 million and holding $17.4 million on hand, while Republican Diamant Hysenaj has raised about $407,000 with roughly $20,000 available. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent, and prediction markets give her roughly a 97 percent chance of winning.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency and fundraising gap, and market pricing. Together these point to a comfortable Democratic win, with the incumbent favored by roughly 26 points. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which leaves some room for error around the size of the margin, though not enough to put the outcome in doubt.
